final_candidates.decision_summary: Conserved RING Zn ligand; near-max AlphaMissense LOF and very low evolutionary/sequence tolerance support functional knockout while likely preserving local folding.
Second strongest LOF signal at another conserved RING Zn ligand; slightly better sequence plausibility balances loss-of-function and folding preservation.
Very high LOF score and strong conservation at a RING Zn ligand; retained despite low sequence_plm because functional ablation is strongly supported.

stop_reason.detail: All available tool calls have been used, and the current evidence is sufficient to finalize the top three candidates.

history.rationale: Known pathogenic RING zinc ligand; loss of Cys61 disrupts E3 ubiquitin ligase/BARD1 function.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
Strong LOF score (0.990) but Cys->Gly may impair folding; kept below aromatic substitutions.
High LOF signal at a conserved Zn ligand; retained as a backup although its LOF score is slightly below the top three.
RING zinc-coordinating residue; C64G is a recurrent pathogenic LOF mutation.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
LOF score lower than the top Cys aromatic variants and Cys->Gly is less fold-preserving.
High LOF and conserved RING position, but lower priority due to very low sequence_plm and slightly lower combined evidence strength.
Zinc ligand in RING domain; substitution likely abolishes BRCA1 tumor-suppressor activity.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
High LOF score (0.993) at conserved zinc-coordinating Cys; Cys->Tyr retains side-chain bulk better than Gly variants.
Very high LOF score and strong conservation at another RING Zn ligand; conservative ranking because sequence_plm is low but not disqualifying.
RING zinc ligand; aromatic substitution disrupts metal coordination and E3 ligase function.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
Highest AlphaMissense LOF score among pool (0.997) at a conserved RING zinc-ligand cysteine; rare substitution is expected for loss of function.

Strongest combined LOF and conservation evidence among active candidates; C47 is a conserved RING Zn ligand, and the near-max AlphaMissense score plus very low evolutionary tolerance support functional ablation.
Zinc-coordinating cysteine; bulky hydrophobic substitution likely impairs RING folding/function.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
Very high LOF score (0.995) and slightly better sequence plausibility than other Cys aromatic swaps, supporting both disruption and moderate fold tolerance.
Second-highest LOF score with slightly better sequence plausibility than other top Zn-ligand cysteines, suggesting a reasonable balance between loss-of-function and folding preservation.
Histidine zinc ligand in RING; substitution removes metal coordination required for function.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
Good LOF score (0.973) and the best sequence plausibility of the pool, so it is retained as a fold-tolerant fallback.
Lower LOF score than top cysteine mutations but better sequence_plm, making it a folding-friendlier fallback if stronger Zn-ligand substitutions risk instability.
N-terminal RING zinc ligand; Gly substitution should abolish zinc binding and E3 activity.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
High LOF score (0.993), but Gly substitution likely destabilizes the RING fold more than aromatic swaps, lowering confidence.
Comparable LOF score to C39Y and extremely low evolutionary tolerance, but lower sequence_plm keeps it below the top three.
RING zinc ligand; loss of Cys27 disrupts domain structure and tumor-suppressor function.
No new evidence yet; retaining this RING zinc-ligand candidate.
High but not top LOF score; Gly substitution carries folding risk.
Still a viable conserved Zn-ligand LOF candidate, but lower LOF score and sequence plausibility place it at the bottom of the active pool.
Buried RING residue near zinc-binding site; may alter local packing and impair function.
No new evidence yet; retaining as a lower-priority conservative candidate.
LOF score is meaningfully lower (0.838) than the top candidates, so it is not competitive for a top-3 LOF design.

rejection.reason: LOF score is meaningfully lower (0.838) than the top candidates, so it is not competitive for a top-3 LOF design.

history.rationale: Adjacent to C64 zinc ligand; proline likely distorts RING conformation and reduces function.
No new evidence yet; retaining as a lower-priority candidate near the RING zinc site.
Despite high LOF score, proline substitution has zero sequence plausibility and is evolutionarily rare, indicating likely fold disruption incompatible with the objective.
